kpi.use: One headline figure, when the total or average is the whole message.
kpi.watch: A bare number means little; add a period or a target.
tips: Round to the precision people need

histogram.use: See how one measure is spread: where most values sit, how skewed, and any stragglers.
histogram.watch: Bin width changes the shape, so try a couple.
tips: Compare median and mean to judge skew

box.use: Compare the middle and spread of a measure across groups.
box.watch: It hides how many rows sit behind each box.
tips: Keep to a handful of groups

density.use: Show where many points overlap, as shaded regions instead of a blur of dots.
density.watch: Shade shows crowding, not exact values.
tips: Use it from a few thousand rows up
Switch to scatter to inspect outliers

line.use: Show how a measure moves over time, or compare a few series.
line.watch: A line implies order, so never join unordered categories. Many lines tangle.
tips: Keep to five lines or fewer

bar.use: Count how many rows fall in each category, largest first.
bar.watch: Many categories make a long axis; show the top ones and group the rest.
tips: Sort by size unless the categories have a natural order

barplot.use: Compare a total or average for each category.
barplot.watch: Bars must start at zero or their lengths mislead.

treemap.use: Show each category's share of a whole when there are too many for bars.
treemap.watch: Area is harder to compare than length, and small labels vanish.
tips: Use it for share, not for precise ranking

heatmap.use: Spot where two categories combine most strongly; darker means more.
heatmap.watch: Colour is approximate. Read exact values from the table.

scatter.use: Test whether two measures rise or fall together, and spot outliers.
scatter.watch: A pattern is not proof of cause, and dense data overplots.
tips: Switch to density past a few thousand rows

bubble.use: Add a third measure to a scatter as dot size.
bubble.watch: People judge area poorly, so keep size differences large.
tips: Label only the dots that matter

correlation.use: A grid of how strongly each pair of measures moves together.
tips: Open a strong pair as a scatter

map.use: Plot rows by latitude and longitude, or shade regions by a value.
map.watch: Dense areas hide points, and large regions look more important than they are.
tips: Zoom to the area of interest

terms.use: See the most frequent words in a text column.
terms.watch: Common words and spelling variants can crowd the list.

pivotHeatmap.use: Colour each cell of a pivot to see highs and lows.
pivotHeatmap.watch: It only makes sense on an already summarised pivot.

dotplot.use: Compare many categories with light marks; the axis need not start at zero.
dotplot.watch: Without a zero baseline, gaps look bigger than they are, so the note names where the axis starts.

stacked100.use: Show how each row splits into shares that always add to 100%.
stacked100.watch: Only the first segment shares a baseline, so later segments are hard to compare.
tips: Put the segment that matters first
Keep to a handful of segments

smallmultiples.use: Give each group its own small line chart when one chart would tangle.
smallmultiples.watch: Separate scales hide differences in size between panels, so read the numbers.
tips: Keep to about a dozen panels

slopegraph.use: Compare two moments for many groups: who rose, who fell, and by how much.
slopegraph.watch: Only the first and last points show; anything in between is hidden.

waterfall.use: Show how steps add up to a total, with gains rising and losses falling.
waterfall.watch: Step order changes the picture, and a total only makes sense for additive measures.

notOffered: No pie charts: slices are hard to compare. Use bars, or a 100% stacked bar when shares are the point.
credit: The ideas here draw on Storytelling with Data, Data to Viz and the FT Visual Vocabulary. Everything is written fresh, and this app makes no outside requests.
